Short facts necessary for the purpose of disposal of this rule are that the opposite-party No. 1 Bangladesh as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 36 of 2010 impleading the petitioners and others as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of its title and for partition. The petitioner entered appearance upon filling written statement thereafter issues were framed by the trial court and the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing. At that stage an application under Order XXIII, rule 1(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed by the plaintiff to withdraw the suit without any permission to sue afresh. Defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4 who are the petitioners before us filed an application for transposition with a prayer for transposing them as plaintiff Nos. 1, 3 and 4 in the suit. 

 "that in the plaint, Government having claimed 0.7831 acres of land of SA Plot Nos. 4236, 4237, 4223 and 4235 as abandoned property and having also prayed for a decree that recording of major portion of the said plots in Rs and Mahanagor Survey in the name of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is illegal and void and the Government having raised direct allegation against the defendant No. 1 and 2 and claim of the plaintiff being diametrically opposite to the defendant, as such defendant cannot be transposed as plaintiffs." 

 17. To elucidate the aforesaid decisions for the purpose of deciding the applicability thereof in the instant case we find that in the instant case before us the plaintiff had prayed for a decree declaring its title in the suit land and .for correction of record of right and also for partition of its claimed land and in view of Order XX, rule 18 Sub-Rule (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure it is evident that while granting a saham to a particular property in a partition suit, it is also incumbent upon the Court concerned to decide the right, title in that particular property for the claimed saham. We have also quoted the written submissions advanced by the learned Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the opposite-party in this Rule. Wherefrom it is evident that claims and counter claims have been made by the parties over the same subject matter of the suit and that has to be decided finally and completely in between the parties and in doing so we find no reason for either party to be prejudiced on the final adjudication of the present suit.
